question: How a progressbartype sprite is loaded and drawn through gfx/FX/progress.fx: the class, its keys, the effect, which technique when, every parameter and its value, the vertices and their texture coordinates (and whether the picture comes out upside down), the rotation, the states, and who sets how full a bar is.

addresses.name: CProgressBarType::CProgressBarType
addresses.comment: **Makes a `progressbartype`** (0x180 bytes; operator new and this call at VA 0xA708E4 in ObjectType_CreateByToken, token 313). **The class has no RTTI** - the dword before its table 0x16068F0 (rva 0x12068F0) is a code address, not a complete object locator - so `CProgressBarType` is a name made from the keyword, not read. It does not call the CSpriteType constructor: it fills the CObjectType part itself (name string +8, string +0x24, +0x48 = 0, +0x4C = 0, +0x50 = 0), stores the graphics at +0x58, empties the effectFile string +0x5C, builds two CColor at +0x78 and +0x94 (vftable 0x15B6914, all four floats 1.0, opaque byte 1), empties the strings +0xB0 (textureFile1) and +0xCC (textureFile2), sets both texture indices +0xE8/+0xEC to -1, zeroes +0xF0..+0xF8, sets `horizontal` +0x120 = 1, `allwaystransparent` +0x174 = 0 and the two texture-coordinate extents +0x178/+0x17C = 1.0. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-progressfx.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xB26CA0..0xB26E16: `mov esi,[ebp+8]` (this), `[esi+0x58] = [ebp+0xc]`, vftable 0x16068F0 written at 0xB26CF6, three 0x40A160 string inits at +0x5C/+0xB0/+0xCC, `or eax,-1` into +0xE8/+0xEC, `[esi+0x120] = 1`, float 1.0 (0x171DBAC) into +0x178/+0x17C, `ret 8`. Caller VA 0xA70903: `push esi(graphics); push eax(new 0x180); call`. No RTTI: dword at 0x16068EC is 0xB205B0 (code); positive control - the same read at 0x15E1D40 gives the locator naming `.?AVCMaskedSpriteType@@`. Wrong if the class name ever turns up in RTTI or a string - none of the image's strings containing 'progress' names a class.

addresses.name: CProgressBarType::DeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: Slot 0 of the progressbartype table 0x16068F0 (rva 0x12068F0): the destructor 0x726E50, then operator delete where `flags & 1`. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xB26E20..0xB26E3E: `call 0xb26e50; test byte [ebp+8],1; je; push esi; call 0xb95f9b` (operator delete), `ret 4`. Table slot 0 read directly at 0x16068F0. Wrong if 0x726E50 is not the destructor (not read).

addresses.name: CProgressBarType::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CProgressBarType::LoadKey(CProgressBarType* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys of a `progressbartype`** (slot 4). Through a byte table at VA 0xB27924 and a jump table at VA 0xB27910 for tokens 0x25..0x55, and compares above: `textureFile1` (0x25) -> string +0xB0 (ParseString), `textureFile2` (0x26) -> string +0xCC, `size` (0x2E) -> two ints +0xF0/+0xF4 (ParseIntPairXY, `{ x = N y = N }`), `color` (0x55) -> the CColor at +0x78 through its slot 3 (CColor::Load), `effectFile` (0x59) -> string +0x5C, `horizontal` (0x96) -> bool +0x120 (ParseBool), `colortwo` (0x133) -> the CColor at +0x94, `allwaystransparent` (0x166) -> bool +0x174. **Every other key goes to CObjectType::LoadKey (0x6F9640)**, so `name`, `loadType` and `norefcount` are accepted and anything else is the unknown-key report. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-progressfx.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xB27820..0xB2790B and the two tables decoded byte by byte (cases 37, 38, 46, 85 live, the rest to the default 0xB278C1); explicit compares 0x59, 0x96, 0x96+0x9D=0x133, 0x133+0x33=0x166. Token names from ghidra/saveTokens.json (37 textureFile1, 38 textureFile2, 46 size, 85 color, 89 effectFile, 150 horizontal, 307 colortwo, 358 allwaystransparent). Default `push eax; push edx; call 0xaf9640`. Wrong if saveTokens.json's numbering is off; it is the table every other LoadKey entry cites.

addresses.name: CProgressBarType::LoadResources
addresses.comment: **Slot 6: the effect, its handles, the two textures and the quad.** In order: `FxHandler_Register(graphics +0x6BCFC, &effectFile, &effectFile, graphics->d3d_device)` - **the string is both path and key**, so every bar naming one file shares one ID3DXEffect; index to +0x11C, the effect (`handler->+4[index-1]`) to +0xF8 (**an index of 0 leaves the effect null and the next line dereferences it**). Handles by name: GetParameterByName(NULL, ...) for `WorldViewProjectionMatrix` (+0xFC), `CurrentState` (+0x100), `vFirstColor` (+0x108), `vSecondColor` (+0x10C), `tex0` (+0x114), `tex1` (+0x118); GetTechniqueByName for `tec0` (+0x104) and `ColorProgress` (+0x110). **`ScrollTech` is never asked for.** +0x178/+0x17C = 1.0. If textureFile1 is not empty: texture index (texture handler `graphics +0x158`, 0x660F30, flag 1) to +0xE8. If textureFile2 is not empty: its index to +0xEC, then 0x6611E0 gives **that file's own width and height**, and +0x178 = w / P(w), +0x17C = h / P(h), P the least power of two not below (`fild`/`fdivp`, the 2^32 correction for an unsigned count). **The extents come from textureFile2, not textureFile1.** Then the four vertices at +0x124 (stride 0x14: x, y, z, u, v) with W = +0xF0, H = +0xF4, U = +0x178, V = +0x17C: positions (0,0), (0,H), (W,0), (W,H), z 0; texture coordinates (0,0), (0,V), (U,0), (U,V) where `horizontal` (+0x120) is set and (0,0), (U,0), (0,V), (U,V) where it is not. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-progressfx.md, sections 2 and 4.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xB26F80..0xB272B7 read whole. Effect vtable offsets +0x24 (GetParameterByName, 9) and +0x34 (GetTechniqueByName, 13) of ID3DXBaseEffect; strings named by disasm.py at 0xB26FBA..0xB2707E. Texture loads 0xB270BE/0xB270E7 into +0xE8/+0xEC guarded by the string lengths +0xC0/+0xDC; size query 0xB270F8 then the power-of-two loops 0xB27110/0xB27145 and fdivp into +0x178/+0x17C. Vertex stores 0xB2717F..0xB272AC: +0x130/+0x134 = 0, +0x16C = U, the `cmp byte [esi+0x120],0` arms swap +0x144/+0x148 against +0x158/+0x15C, +0x170 = V; positions from cvtdq2ps of +0xF0/+0xF4. Wrong if 0x6611E0 answers the padded size rather than the file's - the maskedflag reading of the same handler says the file's own.

addresses.name: CProgressBarType::ReleaseTextures
addresses.comment: Slot 7: hands each texture index that is not negative (+0xE8, then +0xEC) back to the texture handler (`graphics +0x158`, 0x6610E0) and sets it to -1. The effect is kept. The name is inferred from the body; when the slot is called was not read. `ret 4`; the draw 0x727310 begins on the very next byte with no padding (trap 2).
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xB272C0..0xB2730D: two `test ecx,ecx; js` guarded `lea edi,[ebx+0x158]; call 0xa610e0` and `mov [esi+0xe8/0xec], -1`, `ret 4` at 0xB2730D; 0xB27310 opens `push ebx; mov ebx,esp` immediately after (retsBefore from functionStart's 0xB272C0 to 0xB2736F reports that ret). Table slot 7 read directly. The body is confirmed; the name rests on 0x6610E0 being a release, which was not read.

addresses.name: CProgressBarType_Draw
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CProgressBarType_Draw(CProgressBarType* type, CGraphics* graphics, float* world, int progress, CColor* firstColor, CColor* secondColor)
addresses.comment: **The draw.** One caller, CProgressBarObject::Render (0x727AD0). Each call it fetches the effect again from +0x11C into +0xF8 and takes the handles `WorldViewProjectionMatrix`, `CurrentState`, `tec0`, `vFirstColor`, `vSecondColor` by name again. **Technique**: if both texture indices +0xE8 and +0xEC are >= 0 it takes `ColorProgress`, `tex0`, `tex1` by name, SetTechnique(ColorProgress), SetTexture(tex0, the textureFile1 texture) and SetTexture(tex1, the textureFile2 texture) - each the texture handler's entry `graphics +0x15C + index * 0x2C`, null for -1 or an index over 9999; **otherwise SetTechnique(tec0)**, no texture set. Then **`WorldViewProjectionMatrix` = world x identity x D3DXMatrixOrthoRH(screen width +0x6B9BC, screen height +0x6B9C0, 0, 1)**; SetVector(vFirstColor, firstColor r,g,b,a) and SetVector(vSecondColor, secondColor r,g,b,a) from each CColor's +8..+0x14; **SetFloat(CurrentState, (float)(progress / 100.0) x type->+0x178)** - the share scaled by the texture-coordinate extent. Begin(&passes, 0), BeginPass(0), CommitChanges, **SetFVF(0x102 = XYZ | TEX1)**, **DrawPrimitiveUP(TRIANGLESTRIP, 2, type +0x124, stride 0x14)**, CommitChanges, EndPass, End. No render state is set here. `ret 0x18`; the frame is realigned (`push ebx; mov ebx,esp; and esp,-16`), so the arguments are read through EBX. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-progressfx.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xB27310..0xB27745 read whole. Effect vtable offsets: 0xE8 SetTechnique, 0xD0 SetTexture, 0x88 SetVector, 0x98 SetMatrix, 0x78 SetFloat, 0xFC Begin, 0x100 BeginPass, 0x104 CommitChanges, 0x108 EndPass, 0x10C End (ID3DXEffect slots 58, 52, 34, 38, 30, 63-67); device offsets 0x164 SetFVF (89) and 0x14C DrawPrimitiveUP (83). Imports resolved by pefile: 0xD2B408 D3DXMatrixOrthoRH, 0xD2B438 D3DXMatrixMultiply (out=world x identity, then x ortho). Double at 0x160A358 is 100.0. Branch `cmp [esi+0xe8],0; jl 0xb274c8` and the same for +0xEC to the tec0 arm. Wrong if the vtable slot arithmetic is off by one, which the maskedflag reading of the same interface (Begin/BeginPass/CommitChanges at the same offsets) would also be.

addresses.name: CProgressBarObject::CProgressBarObject
addresses.signature: CProgressBarObject* __stdcall CProgressBarObject::CProgressBarObject(CGraphics* graphics@stack:4, CProgressBarObject* this@ESI, CProgressBarType* type@EDI) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The object each element showing a progressbartype owns** (0x198 bytes, no RTTI - its table 0x1606780, rva 0x1206780, is preceded by 0x73, not a locator - so the name is made up). Calls the base constructor 0x6B2770 with this and the screen size packed in two shorts, writes the table, progress +0x14C = 0, rotation +0x150 = 0.0, type +0x154, graphics +0x158, and **copies the type's two CColor** (+0x78 -> +0x15C, +0x94 -> +0x178: token, r, g, b, a and the opaque byte). `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xB27970..0xB27AC0: `mov ebx,[ebp+8]` read as graphics (+0x6B9BC/+0x6B9C0), ESI and EDI used unset (from the caller 0xB2778E: esi = new 0x198, edi = the type), vftable 0x1606780 at 0xB279C7, copies from [edi+0x7c..0x90] and [edi+0x98..0xac], `ret 4`. Wrong if the copied blocks are not the CColor - both are built with vftable 0x15B6914 by the type's constructor.

addresses.name: CProgressBarObject::Render
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CProgressBarObject::Render(CProgressBarObject* this, int arg1, float* world, int arg3, int arg4, int arg5, int arg6)
addresses.comment: Slot 10. Copies the 4x4 matrix it is handed (second argument) and **turns it by the object's rotation (+0x150)**: MakeRotationZ3x3 gives R = [[cos, sin, 0], [-sin, cos, 0], [0, 0, 1]], and the matrix's upper three rows become row x R while its translation row is left alone - so in row-vector terms v' = (x, y, z) R M3 + t: **a bar turns about its local origin, the corner where its fill starts**, x' = x cos - y sin, y' = x sin + y cos. Then CProgressBarType_Draw(type +0x154, graphics +0x158, &turned matrix, progress +0x14C, &first colour +0x15C, &second colour +0x178). The other five arguments are not read. `ret 0x18`. Who calls it, and how the matrix is made from the element's place, was not read.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xB27AD0..0xB27E61 read whole: `mov esi,[ebp+0x10]; rep movsd` x16 into esp+0x48, angle [ebx+0x150] to 0xA5F960 with ESI = esp+0x24 (R), then nine sums of three products each writing esp+0x48..+0x70 (new M0j = sum_k M0k Rkj, checked on M00 and M01), the pushes at 0xB27DE2..0xB27E4C and `call 0xb27310`. Table slot 10 read directly (CShieldObject::Render is slot 10 of its table too).

addresses.name: CProgressBarObject::SetProgress
addresses.comment: **How full a bar is**: slot 23, which the base's slot 24 (0x720540, a `jmp [vftable+0x5C]`) forwards to - and slot 24 is SetFrame on C3dVisibleObject - so **a bar's share arrives through the frame channel**: CIcon slot 18 (0x6A23E0) tail-calls its sprite object's (+0x88) slot 24. progress +0x14C = the argument zero-extended from 16 bits, then 100 where it is above 100. A whole number of hundredths. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: `movzx eax, word [ebp+8]; mov [ecx+0x14c],eax; cmp eax,0x64; jle; mov [ecx+0x14c],0x64; ret 4` at 0xB27E70. Table slot 23 = 0xB27E70 and slot 24 = 0xB20540 (`mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x5c]; jmp eax`) read directly; CIcon table 0x15FFC68 slot 18 = 0xAA23E0 (`mov ecx,[ecx+0x88]; ... jmp [eax+0x60]`). Corroborated by the record's CDiplomacyView surrender bar, which passes 0..100 through icon slot 18.

addresses.comment: Slot 26: `mov ax, word ptr [ecx+0x14c]; ret` - the share SetProgress (slot 23) stored.
addresses.evidence: Body at 0xB27E90; table slot 26 read directly.

addresses.name: CProgressBarObject::GetSize
addresses.comment: Slot 54: writes the type's `size` (+0xF0, +0xF4) into two shorts at `out`. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xB27EA0..0xB27ED3: `mov eax,[ecx+0x154]` (type), +0xF0/+0xF4 into `[out]`/`[out+2]` as words, `ret 4`. Table slot 54 read directly.

addresses.name: MakeRotationZ3x3
addresses.comment: Writes the 3x3 turn about z by `angle` (radians) into nine floats at `out`, row by row: (cos, sin, 0), (-sin, cos, 0), (0, 0, 1) - row-vector convention, so x' = x cos - y sin, y' = x sin + y cos. cos and sin are the CRT's 0x80BCC0 and 0x80BB90. `ret 4`. Used by CProgressBarObject::Render; other callers not looked for.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xA5F960..0xA5FA0C: fld [ebp+8]; call 0xC0BCC0 -> c; call 0xC0BB90 -> s; out+0 = (c, s), out+8 = 0, `fchs` -> out+0xC = (-s, c), out+0x14 = 0, out+0x18 = (0, 0), out+0x20 = 1.0. 0xC0BCC0's x87 path executes `fcos` (0xC0BD2D) and 0xC0BB90's `fsin` (0xC0BBFD), which settles which is which independently of the maskedflag entry's naming.

addresses.name: CColor::Load
addresses.comment: **How a colour is read from a file: `{ r g b }` or `{ r g b a }`** (CColor slot 3). Expects `{`, then three numbers each scanned with `%f` into +8, +0xC, +0x10, **each divided by 255 where it is above 1.0**; alpha +0x14 = 1.0; then, if the next token is not `}`, a fourth number scanned raw into alpha (**not divided by 255**). Sets the opaque byte +0x18 where all four are above 0.999, and expects `}`. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xA62960..0xA62B10: token checks `[+0xc] == 3` ({), `== 0xc` (number) before each `sscanf(text, "%f" (0x15FD134), &field)`, comiss against 1.0 and divsd by 255.0 (0x160A2D0) after each of the first three only, `movss [ebx+0x14], 1.0`, `cmp eax,4` (}) skipping the fourth, comparisons against 0.999 (0x160A2D8) into +0x18, final `== 4`. vtable.py --holding 0xA62960: CColor slot 3 alone.

addresses.name: ParseIntPairXY
addresses.comment: Reads `{ x = N y = N }` - exactly that order, each number scanned with `%i` - into out[0] and out[1]; any other token is the parse-error report 0x67A960. Bare `ret`. The progressbartype `size` key goes through it.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0xA7B670..0xA7B798: token checks 3, 0x1F, 1, 0xC, then sscanf with format 0x15FD14C (`%i`) into [edi]; 0x20, 1, 0xC into [edi+4]; 4; bare `ret`. saveTokens.json: 31 x, 32 y. Caller 0xB27851 sets EAX = parse and EDI = this +0xF0.

addresses.name: CObjectType::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CObjectType::LoadKey(CObjectType* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys every `.gfx` object type shares** - three, not one: `name` (0x1A) -> the string +8; `loadType` (0x14C) -> +0x50 = 1 for `FRONTEND`, 2 for `BACKEND`, 3 for `INGAME`, 0 for anything else; `norefcount` (0x14D) -> bool +0x4C (ParseBool). Any other key is the unknown-key report 0x67A7B0. **It is the base's, not CProvinceType's**: 29 direct calls to it are the fall-through of other types' LoadKeys (the 2D progressbartype's at 0x7278C6 among them), and CProvinceType and CProvinceWaterType hold it at slot 4 because they do not override it. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-progressfx.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Revised: it was CProvinceType::LoadKey, and its comment named `norefcount` only (definitions.py's switch reader missed the `sub eax,0x1a` / `sub eax,0x132` / `dec eax` chain's other two arms). Listing 0xAF9640..0xAF9790: 0x1A -> 0xAF9774 ParseString into +8; 0x14C -> 0xAF96AD ParseString into a local then compared with `FRONTEND` (0x160496C), `BACKEND` (0x1604978), `INGAME` (0x1604980) into +0x50; 0x14D -> 0xAF968F ParseBool into +0x4C; default `call 0xa7a7b0`. saveTokens.json: 26 name, 332 loadType, 333 norefcount. findRefs --callers 0xAF9640: 29 direct calls (0x83BA2D, 0x8450C6, 0x84B755, 0xAB7AA3, 0xB278C6 ...), each a LoadKey's default arm; it is a C2dObjectType's base (progressbartype) and a C3dObjectType's (CProvinceType), so CObjectType. Wrong if some C3d and C2d type do not share CObjectType - RTTI gives both under it.

structs.name: CProgressBarType
structs.comment: A `progressbartype` of the .gfx files: a bar drawn through effectFile (progress.fx in every one the game ships), filled share by share. No RTTI; the name is made from the keyword. Its layout from +8 to +0x50 is CObjectType's (name, loadType, norefcount), filled by its own constructor without the CSpriteType constructor. Table 0x16068F0 (rva 0x12068F0), 26 slots. Its drawn object is a CProgressBarObject. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-progressfx.md.
structs.evidence: operator new(0x180) at VA 0xA708E4 immediately before the constructor 0xB26CA0, which writes 0x16068F0 at [this]. Slot count 26: slot 26 of the run (0xB28450) is followed by 0x45BB10/0x60CD50/0xA7C050, the opening of the next CPersistent-derived table.

structs.name: CProgressBarObject
structs.comment: The object a CProgressBarType makes for each element that shows it (slot 23): how full (+0x14C), its turn (+0x150) and its own copy of the two colours; slot 10 draws it. No RTTI; the name is made up. Table 0x1606780 (rva 0x1206780), 92 slots. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-progressfx.md.
structs.evidence: operator new(0x198) in CProgressBarType::CreateInstance (0xB2776A) before CProgressBarObject::CProgressBarObject, which writes 0x1606780 at [this] (0xB279C7). 92 slots: the type's table follows at 0x16068F0 = 0x1606780 + 92*4.

struct_fields.name: norefcount
struct_fields.comment: `norefcount = yes`. On a sprite type, set: the texture is loaded once in LoadResources and kept; clear: slots 11 and 12 load it on first use and free it on last, counting in +0x48 (FINDINGS-buttonstatefx.md, section 1).
struct_fields.evidence: CObjectType::LoadKey 0xAF968F: token 0x14D, ParseBool into [esi+0x4c].

struct_fields.name: load_type
struct_fields.comment: `loadType`: 1 FRONTEND, 2 BACKEND, 3 INGAME, 0 for anything else or absent.
struct_fields.evidence: CObjectType::LoadKey 0xAF96AD..0xAF974A: three string compares into [esi+0x50] with 1, 2 and (neg/sbb/and 3) 3 or 0.

struct_fields.name: opaque
struct_fields.comment: Set where r, g, b and a are all above 0.999 - by CColor::Load and CColor::Set alike: white more than opaque. Where set, CSpriteType::Draw hands the effect Color = (1, 1, 1, the object's alpha) instead of the colour (FINDINGS-buttonstatefx.md, section 3).
struct_fields.evidence: CColor::Load 0xA62AB2..0xA62AFA: four comisd against 0.999 then `mov byte [ebx+0x18], 1/0`; CColor::Set's entry records the same byte.

struct_fields.evidence: 0x83AC70 `inc dword [ecx+0x48]; ret`; 0x83AC80 `dec dword [ecx+0x48]; jns; mov [ecx+0x48],0; ret`; both at slots 11/12 of 0x16068F0 and 0x15E1D44. Constructor zeroes it at 0xB26CE1.

struct_fields.name: vertices
struct_fields.comment: The quad, four vertices of x, y, z, u, v (stride 0x14), drawn as a triangle strip with FVF XYZ | TEX1: (0,0,0, 0,0), (0,H,0, 0,V), (W,0,0, U,0), (W,H,0, U,V) where horizontal, the u and v of the middle two swapped where not.
